detailCrop.scope: A second genuine native 3D subfrustum render from the unchanged physical reference camera; not an upscaled screenshot.

info.source: Authored three-dimensional architecture and plants with declared CC0 timber and eroded stone scans; no reference-image scene surface

sorin.kind: closed lathe annular plates, rolled rims and continuous central post

hallStair.construction: Twenty closed bearing risers, individually jointed granite tread slabs, weathered nosings, stepped solid cheek courses and connected lower landing

verandaBoards.direction: Z, following recovered veranda edge and bearing plane
verandaBoards.limits: Board end layout and concealed framing are inferred; deck edge and level follow the recovered balustrade.

foregroundRail.kind: one spatial balustrade with closed continuous broad beams and joined inset-panel bays
foregroundRail.limits: Curved plan, 69mm local deck rise and unequal bay lengths are inferred from visible cap/beam axes; the source photograph does not admit perfectly regular perspective.

timber.floorReflection: Actual board clearcoat/PBR roughness and the existing captured scene probe; no spanning mirror plane

scannedGardenStones.author: Kless Gyzen
scannedGardenStones.groundContact: Actual transformed scan minima with a 6.5 percent radius soil embed; no image projection

rootedCanopy.construction: One soil-embedded trunk, seven closed buttress roots, attached tapered boughs and alternate folded leaves; all geometry exists through camera motion

openWaterCorridor.geometry: clear three-metre reflection channel reserved under the bridge and toward the foreground veranda

limits: Visual acceptance pending independent reference comparison.
CC0 scanned timber maps with tracked provenance; no photograph or generated replacement frame is used.
Layout is recovered from visible native contours; source perspective and partly occluded geometry retain uncertainty.
Veranda board end joints and concealed framing are inferred where the source photo does not resolve them.
